summary: Liqian Liu (1910–2008) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at West China Union University (~1946–1949), the translation administration department of the State Council of the People's Republic of China, and the Ethnic Publishing House.

Lisa Grumbach works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She held a post at Stanford University (attested 1996) and has served as an assistant professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Lisa N. Owen is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin under Janice Leoshko and studied under Walter M. Spink in 1995.

Lita Peipina specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Oslo (attested 2008 for her MA), completing her degree under supervisor Jens Braarvig in 2003, and was also taught by Jens-Uwe Hartmann.

Liu Zaifu (1941–2026) was a Sinologist who studied at Xiamen University (~1959–1963). He held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (1963) and the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (~1999).

Lloyd W. Pflueger is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology who completed his doctorate at the University of California, Santa Barbara. He was Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University (attested 2015).

Lobsang Dargyay (1935–1994) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (~1952–1959), and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1970–1974), where he earned his Dr.phil.

Lobsang Gyatso (1928–1997) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. After studying at Drepung Monastery (~1940–1959), he served as Head of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (~1973–1997).

Lobsang Jamspal (born 1936) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1961–1968) and Columbia University (~1974–1991 under Alex Wayman), he held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, University of Delhi, and Columbia.
Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa (1926–2008) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Lobsang Shastri specializes in Tibetology. He served as Head Librarian of the Tibetan Section at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).

Lobsang Tenpa specializes in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He earned a Master of Philosophy at Jawaharlal Nehru University under supervisor Sharad Kumar Soni.

Lobsang Yongdan works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. Educated at Kumbum Monastery and the University of Cambridge (PhD, by 2014, under Hildegard Diemberger), he held postdoctoral posts at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science and University of Bonn.
Loden Sherab Dagyab (born 1940) is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso, and held a post at the University of Bonn (~1966–2004).

Lodrö Sangpo (born 1953) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ernst Steinkellner, founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996, and served as a senior teacher at Gampo Abbey (attested 2008).

Lokesh Chandra (born 1927) is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. After studies under Raghu Vira, at the University of the Punjab, and Utrecht University (PhD ~1949–1950), he served as Secretary (~1950–1963) and Director (~1963) of the International Academy of Indian Culture.
Longlian (1909–2006) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology. She studied under Fazun in 1939 and under Nenghai as a traditional teacher from approximately 1941 to 1967.

Lopon Tenzin Namdak (1927–2025) studied at Menri Monastery (1950–1953) and under Sangye Tenzin, Gangru Tsultrim Gyaltsen, and Sherab Tenzin Gyaltsen. He co-founded Menri and Triten Norbutse Monasteries, serving as chief scholar-in-residence at Menri and Lobpon at Triten Norbutse.

Lore Sander (1936–2023) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1960–1965). She served as Curator at the Museum für Asiatische Kunst (1987) and held positions at Free University of Berlin, Humboldt University, and LMU Munich.

Lori Meeks (born 1976) works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied under Jacqueline I. Stone and Ryuichi Abe, completed a postdoc at Stanford (~2003–2004), and was appointed Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at USC (~2004).
